faqs.q: How do I calculate my cash back?

faqs.a: A flat 2% on everything is simple. Tiered cards pay more in bonus categories like groceries or fuel. Enter both cards' rates here and compare the annual totals for your spending pattern.
Yes, when the balance is paid in full every month. Carrying a balance means interest charges that almost always exceed the rewards earned. Rewards never justify debt.
faqs.q: Is cash back really free money?

faqs.a: Compare the annual rewards against the fee. A $95 fee needs about $95 more in rewards than a free card to break even. This calculator shows the rewards side; subtract the fee yourself.
In most countries, credit card rewards are treated as purchase discounts, not taxable income. Sign-up bonuses tied to spending usually follow the same treatment, but check local rules.
For most people the effective rate lands between 1.5% and 3%. Bonus categories can push it higher, while uncapped flat cards cluster near 2%.
faqs.q: What is a good effective cash-back rate?

cash-back-calculator.formula:
monthly_reward = sum(spend_category x rate_category / 100)
annual_reward = monthly_reward x 12
effective_rate = monthly_reward / total_spend x 100
howTo: Enter your average monthly spending in each category.
Enter the cash-back rate your card pays per category.
Read your monthly and yearly rewards and your effective rate.
Change the rates to compare a different card.
Pick the card with the highest annual total for your pattern.
keyFacts: Cash-back cards return a percentage of each purchase as money, statement credit or points.

cash-back-calculator.quickAnswer: Spending $600 on groceries at 3%, $250 on dining at 2%, $200 on fuel at 3% and $800 elsewhere at 1% earns $37 per month — $444 per year at a 2.00% effective rate.
cash-back-calculator.tagline: See what your spending really earns you.
cash-back-calculator.workedExample:
Groceries $600 x 3% = $18. Dining $250 x 2% = $5. Fuel $200 x 3% = $6. Other $800 x 1% = $8.

Monthly rewards = 18 + 5 + 6 + 8 = $37. Annual rewards = 37 x 12 = $444.

Total spend = 1,850. Effective rate = 37 / 1,850 x 100 = 2.00%.
